en: Points of Controversy,
Great Fifty,
Sixth Chapter
The Discourse on Space:
Is space unconditioned? Yes.
Is Nibbāna a refuge, a shelter, a resort, a final goal, the undecaying, the deathless?
One should not say so... [etc. ...
Is space unconditioned? Is Nibbāna unconditioned?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Are there two unconditioned things?
One should not speak thus … [and so on] … .
Are there two unconditioned things?
Yes. Are there two refuges … [and so on] … or are they intermediate? Yes.
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is space unconditioned? Yes.
Is there anyone who makes what is not space into space?
Yes. Is there anyone who makes the conditioned into the unconditioned? Yes.
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is it the case that there are some who make space non-space? Yes.
Is it the case that some make the unconditioned conditioned?
One should certainly not say so… [as before] … Birds fly in the sky; the moon and sun move; the stars move; [and there is] psychic power.
"Do they perform transformations; do they wave their arms, wave their hands, throw clods of earth, throw clubs, hurl supernatural power, and shoot arrows?
"Yes, they do."
Do winged birds go in the unconditioned? Do the moon and sun go in the unconditioned? Do the forms of the stars go in the unconditioned?
Do they exercise psychic power? Do they move their arms? Do they move their hands? Do they throw clods of earth?
Do they throw clubs? Do they hurl psychic power? Do they hurl arrows?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Do they build houses and construct storehouses by surrounding space? Yes.
"Do they build houses and construct storehouses by surrounding the unconditioned?
"One should not say so...
"...Is it the case that when a well is being dug, the non-space becomes space?"
“Yes,” you say.
“Then does the conditioned become unconditioned?
You must not say so … [and so on].
When an empty well is being filled, when an empty storehouse is being filled, and when an empty jar is being filled, does the space disappear?
Yes. Does the unconditioned disappear?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said that “space is unconditioned”?
“Yes.
“Then space is conditioned?
“One should not say so,” and so forth.
Therefore, space is unconditioned.
The discussion on space is finished.
